summary: In this story, a girl named Sara notices a quiet new classmate who always sits alone, and a small act of kindness turns into a lasting friendship.
introduce: Show the title “The Quiet New Friend” and ask, “What do you think will happen in this story, and why?” Explain that good readers use clues in the text together with what they already know to make inferences.

keyTerms.def: a student who is in the same class as you
the bravery needed to do something hard or scary

challengeTerms.def: the ability to understand and share how someone else feels
slow to act because you feel unsure or nervous
a small action that shows kindness or a feeling

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that it is always worth the risk to reach out to someone who seems lonely, even if they might say no? Use evidence from the story to explain.
Explain why Sara's small action made such a big difference to Lama.
struggling: Read the first part of the story aloud together, review classmate, courage, and awkward, and let weak readers answer “What clue tells you that?” questions using sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses empathy, hesitant, and gesture to make an inference that the story does not state and support it with two clues.
